exercises.name: Left Elbow Flexion
exercises.goal: Gently bend and extend your left elbow to maintain bicep and forearm mobility.

safety_warnings.tilt_warning: Try to keep your shoulders level and avoid leaning sideways.
safety_warnings.elbow_flare_warning: Keep your elbow tucked close to your side instead of lifting it out sideways.
safety_warnings.shrug_warning: Relax your shoulders downward — avoid shrugging to lift your arm.
safety_warnings.speed_warning: Slow down slightly for safe, controlled muscle engagement.

cues.start: Starting Left Elbow Flexion. Face the camera with your left arm hanging straight down and your upper arm pinned to your side, then slowly curl only your hand upward toward your left shoulder, pause, and lower slowly back straight. Say stop anytime.
cues.flexed: Great reach! Hold briefly, then slowly lower your forearm all the way back down.
cues.completed: Exercise complete! Wonderful focus on form and safety.

faq.purpose: This exercise strengthens your left biceps and preserves elbow range of motion without straining your back.
faq.form: Face the camera sitting upright, pin your left upper arm vertically against your ribs, keep your shoulders level, and bend only at the elbow from a straight arm down toward your shoulder without lifting your elbow sideways.

exercises.name: Right Elbow Flexion
exercises.goal: Gently bend and extend your right elbow with steady, controlled posture.

safety_warnings.tilt_warning: Keep your chest upright and avoid compensating by tilting your torso.
safety_warnings.elbow_flare_warning: Keep your elbow tucked close to your side instead of lifting it out sideways.
safety_warnings.shrug_warning: Relax your shoulders downward — avoid shrugging to lift your arm.
safety_warnings.speed_warning: Move smoothly and avoid rushing the return.

cues.start: Starting Right Elbow Flexion. Face the camera with your right arm hanging straight down and your elbow tucked against your ribs, slowly curl your forearm upward toward your right shoulder, then lower back down smoothly.
cues.flexed: Nice control! Slowly lower your arm all the way back to straight.

faq.purpose: Maintains right upper-arm strength and elbow joint flexibility from a seated position.
faq.form: Sit upright facing the camera, pin your right elbow beside your ribcage without flaring it sideways, keep your shoulders relaxed, and curl smoothly from straight to your shoulder.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Raise
exercises.goal: Lift your left arm outward toward shoulder height to build deltoid and upper-back stability.

safety_warnings.tilt_warning: Avoid shrugging or leaning sideways to lift higher; stop at a comfortable height.
safety_warnings.elbow_bend_warning: Keep your arm straighter during the shoulder raise instead of bending your elbow.
safety_warnings.over_elevation_warning: Stop at shoulder height to avoid shoulder impingement.
safety_warnings.speed_warning: Lower your arm gently rather than letting it drop.

cues.start: Starting Seated Shoulder Raise. Sit facing the camera with your left arm straight at your side, slowly lift your straight arm out sideways until it is level with your shoulder like a T shape, pause, and lower gently.
cues.flexed: Great shoulder height! Pause briefly, then lower your arm slowly back to your side.
cues.completed: Shoulder raise session complete! Great posture.

faq.purpose: Builds shoulder stability and upper-torso support important for wheelchair propulsion and transfers.
faq.form: Keep your torso upright without leaning, keep your elbow straight as you lift out sideways, and stop right at shoulder height instead of raising overhead.

exercises.name: Seated Core Reach & Return
exercises.goal: Perform a small, controlled sideways upper-body lean and return to center to engage core stabilizers.

safety_warnings.tilt_warning: Keep the lean small and controlled within your wheelchair balance zone.
safety_warnings.spine_lean_warning: Keep your lean smaller to stay safely balanced in your seat.
safety_warnings.speed_warning: Move slowly so your core muscles stay engaged.

cues.start: Starting Seated Core Reach. Lock your wheelchair brakes, sit tall facing the camera with your hips planted, gently lean your upper body slightly to one side, pause, and return smoothly upright to center.
cues.flexed: Good core engagement! Slowly bring your shoulders back upright and level.

faq.purpose: Trains lateral core and trunk control safely while seated.
faq.form: Ensure brakes are locked, keep both hips planted evenly on your seat, and keep the sideways reach small and controlled within your balance zone.
